title: Networked Polling Terminals
summary: A client/server polling system connecting Raspberry Pi terminals to a central desktop monitoring and reporting application.
problem: Organizations need to collect responses at several locations and review their status and results in one place.
approach: Programmed networked Raspberry Pi client and Python server components.
Built PyQt interfaces for poll setup, device status and live totals.
Added reporting workflows with filters for location, date, time and response.
outcome: A distributed polling application with terminal interfaces, centralized data and an operator reporting workflow.
software: Local buffering & central SQL Server records

sections.title: Terminals and a central operator application
body: Raspberry Pi polling terminals collect responses at different locations. A Windows application creates polls, selects the active poll, monitors device status and displays results.

sections.title: Recording through a disconnection
body: When a terminal loses its network connection, it stores responses locally. After reconnection, queued records are synchronized with the server and transferred local records are cleared. Device time is synchronized periodically from the network/server.

sections.title: Making results useful
body: The Python/PyQt application shows counts and percentages for the full system or an individual terminal, monitors incoming responses and provides reporting filters such as region, date, time and selected option.

sections.title: Seeing the system work
body: The media includes a physical demonstration with five terminals, a simulated workflow and a reporting-interface demonstration. Together, they explain the relationship between the devices, central data and operator controls.

result: A distributed polling application with terminal interfaces, centralized data and an operator reporting workflow.
decisionNotes: Terminals retain responses locally when disconnected, synchronize queued records after reconnection and clear transferred local records. The central application handles poll setup, device monitoring and reporting.
validationNotes: The archive includes a physical five-terminal demonstration, a simulated workflow and a reporting-interface recording. These are demonstration evidence; no election-security assessment or production reliability measurement is supplied.
